- Trust asymmetry is git-correct: shallow grafts only REMOVE parent edges from the commit graph, so a POSITIVE `merge-base --is-ancestor` (exit 0) on truncated history is a fortiori true on full history (reachability is monotone under edge addition); a NEGATIVE (exit 1) can be a graft-cut false negative — exactly what the bullet states, including the verified depth-1 degenerate case (post-filter drops nothing at depth 1).
- Rung ladder syntax valid: `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`; `git fetch --deepen=200 origin main <branch>` (bounded relative deepen); `git fetch --unshallow --filter=blob:none` with the plain `--unshallow` fallback for filter-refusing servers.
